Nothing.

Probably the difficulty is that forwards and replies are formatted inconsistently in many ways and the client resists color configuration of reply text for forwards.

• Neither replies nor forwards observe the dark mode configuration for the body of the email being replied to or forwarded. In both, it appears in quasi-light light mode with various elements appearing in red rectangles, instead of dark mode as in the email received. This is a gross rendering failure.

• Furthermore, and quite oddly, forwards and replies inconsistently configure message text. The first failure is that replies are in dark mode and forwards are in light mode. The second failure is that message text in forwards is white, consistent with the dark mode scheme but not with white background, which is inconsistent with the dark mode scheme. The third failure is that the client resists configuration of message text to to any other color. So, perhaps a signature exists in the forwards but becase of this cascade of color configuration failures, is invisible.

content:
Please check your computer to see if you have got a VPN enabled. Many Anti-virus products now off a VPN and in some cases it's been auto enabled. Most servers do not like a VPN because it hides your IP address, so server thinks you might be a hacker. Server decides to protect your account and blocks access.

Maybe Anti-Virus is intervening as it scans any file that gets opened etc and causing an initial delay in connection, but soon after a connection is made.

Maybe you still have an old account trying to connect to a server.

  • Settings > Privacy & Security
  • Scoll to Passwords section
  • click on 'Saved Passwords'

Are there any references to any old accounts you have since removed ? If yes, select relevant lines and click on 'Remove'

Maybe you also have a Calendar or address book to another server eg: gmail Maybe that pop up is not for email, but for a calendar ?

This happens when the headers are included in your forwarded emails. The headers include long blocks of information like received from, signature, return path, and much more info that a recipient doesn’t need.
